report.summary: Chunk 6 of 6: defines spectral_evidence function and the tail of analyse's return dict. No public symbols beyond the function. Claims about behaviour are verified against visible code.

symbols.name: spectral_evidence
symbols.note: Flattens analyse reading into per-module evidence rows

claims.text: The picker enriches an EXISTING candidate's evidence with these; it never creates a candidate from them and never lets them move a band.
claims.why: Refers to behaviour of 'the picker' which is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: A module that is not in the graph gets no row, so a caller that looks one up gets nothing rather than a zero that reads like a measurement.
claims.why: The function computes modules from partition and values; if a module is absent from both, it is not added to out. The return dict will have no entry for that module.

claims.text: spectral_fiedler_value is None for a module outside the Fiedler scope (an island, or any node off the largest component). None means NOT MEASURED -- never 0.0, which would read as 'sits on the seam'.
claims.why: The line `'spectral_fiedler_value': values.get(module)` uses .get() which returns None if module is not in values. The docstring's claim about None vs 0.0 is upheld by this code.

claims.text: Flatten a full analyse() reading into per-module evidence rows.
claims.why: The function takes a reading dict and returns a dict mapping module to a dict of evidence fields. This matches the description.

observations.what: The function spectral_evidence uses reading.get('available') to early-exit if not available.
The function builds a set of modules from partition values and falls back to values keys if partition is empty.
The function iterates over sorted modules and constructs a per-module dict with fields like spectral_package, spectral_package_leak_rate, etc.
